purpose: bounded prior-art and benchmark audit; not a global novelty theorem
project_definition_status: R54 five-view definition and R7-R9 legacy robustness supplied by parent repository census; not independently re-audited by this literature reviewer

search_scope.second_pass: Same reviewer, independent SciSpace and Parallel discovery plus primary-source extraction
blind_spots: Several sources inspected by targeted excerpts, not complete derivation audit

sources.title: Multipole Vectors—a new representation of the CMB sky and evidence for statistical anisotropy or non-Gaussianity at 2<=l<=8
sources.checked: primary search extraction, not full proof audit
sources.result: Each real multipole is represented by l headless unit vectors and a scalar amplitude, nonlinearly related to a_lm and transforming covariantly under rotations.
sources.implication: Vector/tensor-valued morphology alone is prior art. Compare low-l orientation, area-vector alignment and power as separate benchmark outputs.
sources.missing_bridge: The project's five-variable mapping and statistical calibration must be compared on identical maps/masks.

sources.title: The Cosmic Microwave Background Bipolar Power Spectrum: Basic Formalism and Applications
sources.locator: BipoSH covariance expansion; BiPS definitions around equations 23–25
sources.checked: primary full-text excerpt acquired; covariance representation inspected
sources.result: BipoSH irreducibly decomposes the harmonic covariance, including off-diagonal correlations; BiPS contracts this into rotational invariants. Beam/noise/masks can produce signals.
sources.implication: A matrix-valued a_lm covariance tensorization must be benchmarked against the same retained BipoSH sectors, not against C_l alone.
sources.missing_bridge: Define empirical vs ensemble covariance and calibrate one-sky estimators, masks and anisotropic noise.

sources.title: Multipole decomposition of the general luminosity distance 'Hubble law'—a new framework for observational cosmology
sources.checked: primary text; conventions, photon-direction sign and Hubble decomposition inspected
sources.result: For c=1 and k=E(u-e), H(e)=Theta/3-a.e+sigma:ee. The local distance-redshift expansion has 9/25/61 coefficients through first/second/third order.
sources.implication: Directional Hubble kinematics already has a physical tensor map. Restore c and distinguish the parameter vector theta from expansion scalar Theta. Vorticity is absent from the first-order slope but enters higher-order coupled terms.
sources.missing_bridge: A finite-redshift likelihood still needs convergence range, derivatives/closure, noise/selection and observer-frame treatment.

sources.title: Covariant cosmography: the observer-dependence of the Hubble parameter
sources.checked: requested v2 HTML was resolved by provider to full text explicitly labelled v3; v3 recorded as inspected version
sources.result: For dust matter, the matter-frame physical Hubble parameter has monopole and shear quadrupole. Observer boost produces a dipole including shear-dependent aberration. Incorrect luminosity-distance transformations can create spurious octupoles.
sources.implication: A fitted Hubble dipole cannot be assigned to global tilt before applying the correct observer-frame transformation. Dust result does not eliminate acceleration dipoles for arbitrary congruences.
sources.missing_bridge: Implement an explicit convention-consistent frame map and avoid combining formulas for different congruences.

sources.title: First constraints on the intrinsic CMB dipole and our velocity with Doppler and aberration
sources.checked: primary targeted text extracted through independent Exa and Parallel routes; SciSpace discovery cross-check
sources.result: Delta1=beta+Delta_int, betaD=beta+(1+alphaNG)Delta_int, betaA=beta+Ld. The general parameterization has 9 observable components and 10 unknowns. Constraints on intrinsic dipole use a standard dipolar-lensing assumption.
sources.implication: Separating dipole/aberration/modulation is existing work. Conditional nuisance handling, shared-data covariance and identifiability are mandatory in a new tilt likelihood.
sources.missing_bridge: Global tilt requires its own dynamical transfer model; intrinsic dipole is not itself a global tilt measurement.

companion.title: Disentangling Doppler modulation, aberration and the temperature dipole in the CMB
companion.result: Independent calibrated aberration/Doppler estimators; mask, beam, noise, leakage and intensity-to-temperature artifacts are modeled.

sources.title: Interpreting the CMB aberration and Doppler measurements: boost or intrinsic dipole?
sources.checked: primary abstract authenticated; detailed derivation not audited
sources.result: Doppler-like boost and intrinsic-potential couplings can be degenerate under single-field-inflation second-order initial conditions; aberration-like lensing is generally distinct but can be fine-tuned to a boost.
sources.implication: No unconditional observational separation theorem should be claimed from a preferred direction or dipole alone.
sources.missing_bridge: Exact tilt model and its projected templates must be shown distinguishable in the actual data likelihood.

sources.title: How isotropic is the Universe?
sources.locator: Anisotropic models; near-isotropic shear modes; ABSolve construction
sources.checked: primary text inspected for model classes and linearization
sources.result: Tests small anisotropy in I, V, VII0, VIIh via scalar/vector/tensor shear modes and temperature/polarization patterns. Closed IX is not included in the analyzed family.
sources.implication: A shear-eigenvalue label is a local morphology classification, not a Bianchi Lie-algebra classification. A new model-family likelihood must retain class-dependent structure/evolution and transfer templates.
sources.missing_bridge: Do not extend published constraints to all tilted Bianchi classes or nonlinear anisotropy.

sources.title: Planck 2018 results. VII. Isotropy and statistics of the CMB
sources.locator: Sections 1, 4, 6.1; null tests and global significance
sources.checked: publisher targeted text extracted; arXiv metadata cross-checked
sources.result: Large-angle temperature anomalies are confirmed; their significance depends on a-posteriori choices. Simulations reproduce the analysis selection, and some analyses use global statistics calibrated by repeating scans on simulations.
sources.implication: Six topic searches, axes, multipole bands, redshift cuts and compression settings need one declared family of global tests; five-variable p-values are not independent simply because named differently.
sources.missing_bridge: Use the project's existing usable simulations and freeze selection before final observed-sky scoring.

sources.title: Generalized massive optimal data compression
sources.locator: Section 2.2, equations 4–7; Gaussian score equation 17; limitations
sources.checked: primary text; local expansion and Fisher optimality inspected
sources.result: The score supplies one summary per parameter and preserves local Fisher information at the fiducial point under regularity assumptions. Gaussian score combines mean-sensitive linear and covariance-sensitive quadratic terms.
sources.implication: Tensorization cannot claim more Fisher information than the correctly specified full likelihood. A new contribution must be demonstrated as information retention, calibration, cost or robustness against specified alternatives.
sources.missing_bridge: Five-variable compression is not automatically sufficient; measure retained Fisher spectrum and simulation-based coverage beyond the fiducial point.

sources.title: Potential signature of a quadrupolar Hubble expansion in Pantheon+ supernovae
sources.checked: primary excerpt acquired; result definition inspected
sources.result: Simultaneously fits Hubble quadrupole and deceleration dipole; results depend on redshift frame and peculiar-velocity corrections.
sources.implication: Use direct STF regression with survey covariance as a baseline; compare the same pre-existing catalog, mask and correction conventions before claiming a new physical measurement.
sources.missing_bridge: Only run this benchmark if a suitable redshift/distance catalog and covariance already exist in the project.
